//: Inkwash · a LIGHT theme: paper panels over a digital ink-wash painting.
//1: THE source for every shell surface (quickshell/: bar, launcher, OSD, power
//2: menu). No upstream palette — every role is lifted from the wallpaper
//3: itself: the white-grey paper, the smoke wash, the olive-black armor, the
//4: gold filigree, the green cape, the cyan burst, the one red sigil. `tokens`
//5: names each role after what it is in the painting so the mapping stays
//6: traceable. theme.lua still owns WINDOW chrome (gaps, border, blur, shadow);
//8: Two-tone rule, ink edition: the GOLD FILIGREE is the frame, the OLIVE INK
//9: of the armor is the readout (a second, greener ink next to the black text),
//10: and the CYAN BURST is the launcher — the one lit thing in the picture goes
//11: to the one surface that covers the bar — printed to its own deep water,
//12: because the launcher's selected row is the launcher color on an 18% tint of
//13: itself over paper, and the burst as painted (#2a8ca6) stops reading there
//14: (2.4:1); the deep water holds 3.6:1. The raw burst survives as a FILL
//15: (cava, btop's download ramp, the terminal's selection and bright cyan).
//16: readoutBright IS declared, unlike graphite: the gold cannot carry a paper
//17: digit (2.1:1), so a solid-`frame` block would be an unreadable active
//18: workspace. With a lifted olive declared, modules/Workspaces.qml draws the
//19: lozenge instead — olive ink with a paper digit (5:1) and an ink rim — which
//20: is what a marked station looks like in ink anyway. Gold stays the frame.
name: inkwash
//tokens: What in the painting -> role, so a palette bump stays traceable.
//print: Derived inks the terminal-side files share, because the filigree's gold (2.4:1) cannot carry TEXT on paper: gold ink #8a6a2a is `frame` printed down to 4.6:1. Gold stays for lines, fills and the cursor block. The burst needs no second ink — `launcher` already IS its deep water (5.7:1 on paper); the burst as painted, #2a8ca6 (3.6:1), is the lit source it was printed from and appears only as a fill.
//quiet: `dim` and `dormant` are two smoke weights, not a weight and a tint: on paper the quiet greys have to be DARKER than they look right, because every surface that carries them is near-white. `dormant` is the launcher's secondary type (generic names, the placeholder) and the resting power glyph at 60%, so it is printed to 3.1:1 on the launcher window and 3.7:1 on an island — the thin smoke (#a3a398, 2.3:1) read as nothing there.
//effects: Flat ink: no glow (nothing is lit on paper but the burst, and that is a fill, not a halo), no scanlines (paper has no raster).
//bar: Bar identity. Paper islands: near-opaque white paper, a 1px gold rim at 80%, small 6px corners — a brush edge, not glass. Opaque-ish on purpose: the painting frosted through a light fill goes muddy, so the fill is paper and the figure stays outside it.
//launcher: Launcher identity: a 1px deep-water rim (the burst, printed) around a paper sheet, 8px window, 5px input + rows.
//osd: OSD identity: a small-cornered paper slip with a 1px gold rim, olive-ink track. No pill — nothing here is a lozenge.
//session: Power-menu identity: paper tiles with 8px corners and a 1px gold edge at 80%, over a light scrim.
//wallpaper: Shared by hyprlock.conf (brightness) and sddm/Main.qml (1 - brightness scrim). 0.92, not 0.55: the painting is a light field, and the dark themes' dim would turn the paper grey — the lock and the greeter are read with ink on paper, not cream on dusk.
